raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On Intel XPU, `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6` sometimes answers an image question with `!` repeated until the output limit. On POPE, 126 of 9000 answers came back like this. The affected questions change on every server restart, but stay the same within one server.

Cause:
- The Idefics2 vision encoder pads the image slices in a batch to one common length, `(bsz, seq_len)`. `cu_seqlens`, however, holds the real slice lengths.
- `VisionIntelXPUAttention` passed the padded `q/k/v` and those `cu_seqlens` to `flash_attn_varlen_func`.
- So every slice after a padded one attended over the wrong rows. The real rows past `cu_seqlens[-1]` were never written; the kernel output comes from `new_empty`, so they keep leftover memory.
- When that memory holds NaN, the logits become NaN and argmax returns token 0 (`!`).
- The encoded image is cached, so every question on that image fails until the server restarts.

## Modifications

- `VisionIntelXPUAttention.forward`: when `bsz > 1` and the row count differs from `cu_seqlens[-1]`:
  1. gather the real rows,
  2. run the varlen kernel on the packed tensors,
  3. scatter the result back into a zero-initialized padded output.
  `VisionAscendAttention` already handles this layout the same way (see also #43748).
- No other path changes. `bsz == 1` (packed encoders such as Qwen-VL) skips the check entirely. Unpadded batches still make the original single kernel call.
- New test `test_xpu_attn_padded_batch_attends_within_each_image` in `test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. It uses slice lengths 1036/1014/1014 and head_dim 72, from a failing MiniCPM-o batch. It fails on main and passes with this change.

Note for reviewers: the `fa3`, `fa4` and `triton_attn` vision backends receive the same padded layout with packed `cu_seqlens`. This PR does not change them.

## Accuracy Tests

lmms_eval `pope` on `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6`: full set (9000), seed 42, Intel Arc Pro B60, tp-size 2.

| | pope_accuracy | pope_f1_score | `!!!!` answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 86.84 | 87.29 | 126 |
| this PR | **88.09** | **87.30** | **0** |
| H200 reference (CUDA, tp-size 1) | 88.09 | 87.28 | 0 |

```bash
sglang serve --model-path openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6 --device xpu --tp-size 2 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --trust-remote-code --enable-multimodal --attention-backend triton
python3 -m lmms_eval --model openai \
  --model_args model_version=openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6,num_concurrent=16 \
  --tasks pope --batch_size 16 --seed 42
```

Unit test on B60: `pytest test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. On main: 1 failed, 4 passed. With this PR: 5 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Only padded batches of more than one image (`bsz > 1`) take the new path. That path adds one gather/scatter of q/k/v per encoder layer. POPE end to end took about 12 min both before and after (12:11 vs 12:32, on separate server runs).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -1044,6 +1044,17 @@ def forward(
         )
         if s_aux is not None:
             fa_kwargs["sinks"] = s_aux
+        if bsz > 1 and q.shape[0] != int(cu_seqlens[-1]):
+            # rows are padded per image to seq_len while cu_seqlens holds the real lengths
+            seq_lens = cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]
+            valid = (
+                torch.arange(seq_len, device=q.device)[None] < seq_lens[:, None]
+            ).flatten()
+            output = q.new_zeros(q.shape[0], q.shape[1], v.shape[-1])
+            output[valid] = flash_attn_varlen_func(
+                q[valid], k[valid], v[valid], **fa_kwargs
+            )
+            return output
         output = flash_attn_varlen_func(q, k, v, **fa_kwargs)
 
         return output

@@ -1,7 +1,10 @@
+import itertools
 import sys
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 
 import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
 
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention import vision
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
@@ -51,5 +54,31 @@ def test_xpu_backend_selection_priority(
     assert backend == expected
 
 
+def test_xpu_attn_padded_batch_attends_within_each_image():
+    """Images padded to a common seq_len with real lengths in cu_seqlens must each
+    attend only over their own rows, and the padding rows must come back zero."""
+    lens = [1036, 1014, 1014]
+    bsz, seq_len, heads, head_dim = len(lens), max(lens), 16, 72
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+        [0, *itertools.accumulate(lens)], dtype=torch.int32, device="xpu"
+    )
+    q, k, v = (
+        torch.randn(bsz * seq_len, heads, head_dim, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for _ in range(3)
+    )
+
+    out = vision.VisionIntelXPUAttention().forward(
+        q=q, k=k, v=v, cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens, bsz=bsz, seq_len=seq_len
+    )
+
+    for b, n in enumerate(lens):
+        rows = slice(b * seq_len, b * seq_len + n)
+        ref = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            *(t[rows].transpose(0, 1).float() for t in (q, k, v))
+        ).transpose(0, 1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out[rows].float(), ref, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        assert (out[b * seq_len + n : (b + 1) * seq_len] == 0).all()
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
